Primary neuronal-glial brain tumor; raised intracranial pressure does not establish separate ocular disease.
Connective soft tissue neoplasm with fibromyxoid stroma; no other organ of origin is specified.
Bacterial infection umbrella spanning multiple sites; no single anatomical organ is consistently affected across the group.
Malignant germ cell tumor arising in the stomach.
Inherited bile-handling disorder classified under inborn bilirubin metabolism disorders; cholestasis and hepatic fibrosis dominate. Pruritus alone adds no skin axis.
Glycosylation synthesis defect; neurodevelopmental dysfunction in most, hepatic dysfunction and intrinsic coagulation-factor abnormalities commonly exceed 30%; subtype variability.
Inherited platelet disorder with macrothrombocytopenia and impaired aggregation; petechiae reflect bleeding rather than primary skin damage.
Limb synostoses and syndactyly define syndrome; nail absence in 80-99%; renal agenesis in 4/12, with additional renal hypoplasia. Dental findings individually below 30%.
Developmental brain disease and characteristic skin lesions define syndrome; hypogonadism and ptosis each 80-99%. Hypospadias also common, omitted at cap; murmur alone lacks damage.
Focal epilepsy syndrome; its benign, transitory course does not change its neurologic location.
Rotavirus infection primarily damages intestinal enterocytes and causes gastroenteritis.
Autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease; oral ulceration occurs in 30-79%. Associated intestinal inflammation and neoplasms are separate diseases.
Inherited ileal bile acid transport defect disrupts enterohepatic bile acid handling and causes chronic diarrhea and fat malabsorption.
Skeletal and anterior eye defects define this glycosylation disorder; hydronephrosis reported in 1/1, with limited frequency evidence. Recurrent pneumonia is a separate infection.
EBV-associated cutaneous T-cell lymphoma: skin is the tumor site, lymphocytes the malignant cells, and lymphoma supplies the immune mechanism axis.
Psychosocial deprivation causes growth failure with functional suppression of growth hormone secretion; the defining disease phenotype is endocrine.
Abnormal adrenal or gonadal steroid production defines this endocrine and steroid metabolism disorder.
Complex congenital cardiac defects and asplenia define syndrome; asplenia in 5/5 entails loss of splenic blood and immune functions. Abnormal organ position alone adds no axis.
Insufficient functional small intestine causes intestinal failure. Nutritional deficiencies are secondary; cholestasis and thrombosis are minority complications.
Peripheral axonal neuropathy; associated gammopathy alone does not establish immune causation or blood-organ damage. Frequent muscle atrophy is secondary to denervation.
Aldosterone synthesis deficiency causes salt wasting and electrolyte abnormalities; renal sodium loss reflects hormone deficiency rather than intrinsic kidney damage.
Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy; cardiac involvement documented in 16/16.
Umbrella disorder defined by abnormal structure or function of skin or subcutaneous tissue; additional organs depend on the subtype.
